title: 2 Corinthians Bible Quiz - Chapter 2
description: Ten questions on 2 Corinthians 2: the letter written with many tears, forgiving and comforting the one who caused sorrow, and the sweet aroma of Christ.

questions.text: What had the writer determined for himself about his next visit?
questions.explanation: He determined for himself that he would not come to them again in sorrow.

answers.text: That he would not come to them again in sorrow
That he would never write to them again
That he would send Titus in his place
That he would stay away until the winter

questions.text: In what state of mind does he say he wrote to them?
questions.explanation: He says that out of much affliction and anguish of heart he wrote to them with many tears.

answers.text: In great confidence and calm, without any grief
In silence, sending no words of his own at all
Out of much affliction and anguish of heart, with many tears
In anger, to condemn them for what they had done

questions.text: What does he urge them to do with the one whose punishment was sufficient?
questions.explanation: He says they should rather forgive him and comfort him, so that he would not be swallowed up with his excessive sorrow.

answers.text: Hand him over to the assembly of Macedonia
Forgive him and comfort him
Punish him a second time
Keep silent about the matter

questions.text: What does verse 8 beg them to do toward that person?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 says: Therefore I beg you to confirm your love toward him.

answers.text: To write to him about the matter
To send him away from the assembly
To test him with questions first
To confirm their love toward him

questions.text: Why does he say he wrote to them, according to verse 9?
questions.explanation: He says he wrote so that he might know the proof of them, whether they are obedient in all things.

answers.text: So that they would send him a gift for the saints in Jerusalem
So that they would stop grieving over the whole matter
So that he might know the proof of them, whether they are obedient in all things
So that they would commend him to others in writing

questions.text: Why does he forgive, according to verse 11?
questions.explanation: He forgives so that no advantage may be gained over them by Satan, for they are not ignorant of his schemes.

answers.text: So that no advantage may be gained over them by Satan
So that the assembly may grow in number
So that he will not have to come to Corinth
So that Titus may be sent to them

questions.text: What happened when he came to Troas for the Good News of Christ?
questions.explanation: He says that when he came to Troas for the Good News of Christ, a door was opened to him in the Lord.

answers.text: He was put in prison there
A door was opened to him in the Lord
He found Titus waiting for him
He was sent on to Judea

questions.text: Where did he go after he found no relief for his spirit because Titus was not there?
questions.explanation: Because he did not find Titus, his brother, he took his leave of them and went out into Macedonia.

answers.text: To Ephesus
To Corinth
To Jerusalem
Into Macedonia

questions.text: What does God reveal through them in every place, according to verse 14?
questions.explanation: Verse 14 says God always leads them in triumph in Christ and reveals through them the sweet aroma of his knowledge in every place.

answers.text: The sweet aroma of his knowledge
The tablets of stone
The veil of the old covenant
The riches of their generosity

questions.text: How does the chapter contrast the writer and his companions with the many?
questions.explanation: He says they are not as so many, peddling the word of God, but as of sincerity, as of God, in the sight of God, they speak in Christ.

answers.text: They write letters, while the many speak in person
They speak in sincerity in Christ, not peddling the word of God like so many
They take payment, while the many serve for free
They keep silent, while the many preach
